messages:
sara: :rotating_light: incident-bot just paged us — unusual surge of embedding requests to /v1/embeddings from many ephemeral IPs, ~6.8x baseline at the edge. Seeing 429s and token accounting spikes.
incident-bot: [ALERT] route_anomaly: embeddings_request_rate spike detected at 2024-06-21T09:12:01Z. Suggested runbooks: rate_shaping, waf_inspect, disable_batching.
leo: Oncall responding. I’m seeing identical x-client-hash headers across a high-churn IP set, plus a high proportion of unauth requests. Could be scraper bot farm + token stuffing.
mike: Netflow shows concentrated load from APAC edge POPs with proxy churn patterns. Also noticing a small but consistent uptick in api_key reuse for short-lived keys.
sara: Proposed immediate actions: 1) flip WAF rule to block the suspicious header fingerprint (but start in monitor for 3m) 2) apply regional token-based rate_slices 3) disable embeddings batch endpoint (not single-item calls) 4) notify CS + create allowlist for impacted paying tenants.
nina: I’ll handle WAF. I’ll create a monitor rule first and watch false positive rate. Running match expression now.
ops-bot: Runbook step initiated: disable_embeddings_batch queued (ETA 40s).
mike: Drafting a conservative rate-slice — token-weighted to protect big customers. Suggest: per-route slice 15% for anonymous requests in APAC, roll to EU if effective. Fallback is 429 for excess.
(snip) mike: Proposed config:
```
route: /v1/embeddings
region: apac
condition: request.auth == null
action: rate_slice(percent=15, window=60s)
fallback: 429
```
sara: Good. Leo, prioritize keeping enterprise orgs out of the slice. Jamie, can CS prepare a quick notice to top customers in APAC/EU?
jamie: Notifying top 12 embedding customers now with the pre-approved template. Will do targeted outreach if any SLA breaches show up.
leo: WAF in monitor for 3m: https://console/waf/rules/2091 — matching ~12k reqs/min with high churn IPs.
nina: Flipped monitor -> block after 3m, false positives <1%. Blocks for header fingerprint now active in APAC.
ops-bot: Applied rate-slice to APAC region. ID: rs-20240621-ap-7.
sara: Initial telemetry: APAC p95 latency for embeddings decreased ~30% after the rate-slice + WAF block. Good signal.
mike: Disabling batch endpoint globally in 5s (keeping single-item embedding path enabled). Command run: `opsctl endpoints disable --name embeddings_batch --reason "mitigation: scraper fanout"`.
ops-bot: embeddings_batch endpoint disabled.
leo: Quick check for false positives: any paying orgs seeing unexpected 429s?
jamie: One small paying dev org (org-8812) reported CI failures hitting embeddings. I’ve created an allowlist entry and restored their flows. Sent customer note.
sara: Add org-8812 to the runtime allowlist and exempt them from anonymous slices.
mike: Allowlist added: `allowlist add org-8812 --scope embeddings`.
leo: Security question: do we have evidence of credential stuffing (valid token reuse) vs anonymous scraping?
mike: Partial evidence: short-lived tokens being used repeatedly from the same fingerprint set; I’ve flagged keys for rotation and created INF ticket to rotate any high-churn keys older than 24h.
nina: Ops ticket created: INF-9911 to automate WAF fingerprint propagation and include an urgent allowlist flow for CS.
sara: Next steps: keep WAF block and rate-slice for 45m, keep batch disabled for 60m, CS to track SLA deviations, engineering to observe for token reuse pattern and rotate keys if needed.
leo: I’ll prepare a short blameless postmortem checklist — include improving header fingerprint heuristics, smarter per-tenant dynamic quotas, and an automated allowlist path.
ops-bot: Runbook state: mitigations applied. Severity: elevated_contained. Next summary in 30m or sooner if status changes.
ameer: Acknowledged takeover for overnight oncall. I’m paged and have dashboard links + current mitigations. Ping me on PagerDuty if anything flips.
sara: Thanks all. We’ll reconvene for post-incident review tomorrow and turn the temporary mitigations into tracked follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
